dispute_type: Cattle Trespass & Standing Mustard Crop Damage

input.raw_vernacular_audio_or_text: Padosi ki chaar bhains khuli chhoot kar humare sarson ke khet me ghus gayi aur do bigha fasal raund kar barbad kar di. Hazaar rupya ka nuksaan bhugatna pada hai.

expected_transcription.original_text: Padosi ki chaar bhains khuli chhoot kar humare sarson ke khet me ghus gayi aur do bigha fasal raund kar barbad kar di. Hazaar rupya ka nuksaan bhugatna pada hai.
expected_transcription.english_text: The neighbor's four buffaloes were left untethered, entered my mustard field, and trampled two bighas of standing crop, causing thousands of rupees in crop damage.

expected_statutory_matches.section: Section 10 & 24: Impounding Cattle and Compensation for Damage to Land and Produce
expected_statutory_matches.text_snippet: Owners of livestock that trespass and damage standing agricultural crops are liable to pay compensation for the loss occasioned thereby.

expected_draft_output.grievance_summary: Agricultural dispute involving crop damage caused by untethered buffaloes trespassing into a standing mustard field.

applicable_sections.section: Section 10: Cattle Causing Damage to Land
applicable_sections.text_snippet: Provides mechanism for assessing agricultural damage and voluntary restitution.

expected_draft_output.settlement_draft:
1. The cattle owner agrees to pay ₹2,500 as voluntary ex-gratia compensation for damaged mustard produce within 10 days.
2. The cattle owner commits to keep all livestock properly tethered and erect a perimeter fence around his animal enclosure.
3. The petitioner agrees to close the matter without approaching the police cattle pound or registering a formal complaint.
